active_group_PR.title: T-2374, T-2376, T-2380: refine three early Chicago buildings

open_differences.what: The actual rebuilt comparison now shows slimmer 0.60 m square shafts in place of the former 0.90 m blocks. Their complete proportions and heads still differ from the picture: the retained ridge +0.55 m tops remain plain, while Andreas draws slender capped brick stacks. This is a visible narrowing increment, not acceptance of the complete chimney silhouette.

The rebuilt rear-wing roof now physically reaches the main ridge, closing the former short junction. The actual current two-building comparison still differs from Andreas in the broad compound roof silhouette and rear-left gable exposure. This junction increment does not qualify those proportions. Surveyed placement, footprint, pitch and heights remain unchanged; the diagnostic annex camera supplies no independent hotel dimensions.

The rest of the left group still differs from Andreas: the shoulder's own roof slope and eaves line, and the relative proportions of shoulder, connector and farther turned range against the main block. The sharper dormer cap above does not settle them. No new metric distance, height, angle or historical camera is inferred from the provisional fit, and this partial increment is not picture acceptance for the view or for original T-2376.

The plate shows the log jail's own log walls and roof standing well clear above the fence, left of the keeper house. In this render the core is concealed behind the palisade and almost none of it reads. A visitor comparing the two would notice the jail itself is missing from the picture's dominant position: the palisade is too high for the core against this picture, or the core too low, and this increment resolves neither.

The compound's relative proportions are wrong against the plate: the palisade fills most of this render's frame while the plate's fence is a secondary element behind a dominant building group. This follows from the uncalibrated diagnostic camera as much as from the geometry, and no metric error is claimed from it.

The keeper house's drawn elevation is the north front and east gable of the reconstructed `keeper_gale_1902` layout. Whether the plate's house is the same building seen the same way is not established — the plate is captioned 1836 and Andreas draws a different elevation entirely.

Tone and material: the render's palisade reads as one flat dark brown mass, where the plate draws light vertical boards with visible joints and shadow. No board-by-board palisade stock is modelled and none is claimed.

The plate shows the log jail's log gable rising above the plank fence immediately beside the keeper house. In this render the core is concealed behind the palisade and does not read at all. Same unresolved core-exposure question as the Gale view.

Scale and placement in frame differ grossly: the plate's jail group stands close behind the courthouse at the right of a near view, while the render puts the compound small and far off at the right edge. The camera here is diagnostic_only and was never solved to this plate, so this is a framing difference and is not promoted to a geometry error.
The plate draws a light plank fence of separate boards; the render's palisade is one flat dark mass. No per-board stock is modelled and none is claimed.

The camera is the T-3040 initial landmark fit, reused here unchanged so that the before and after differ only by the blockhouse's bytes. It reached its imposed 100 m eye bound and renders the whole compound aerial and undersized against a nearly level printed view; both stockade endpoints are cropped. It is marked diagnostic_only and is not an accepted historical viewing position. Scale, height and framing still want fitting before anything here is judged pixel for pixel. Nothing was moved to fit it.

The print shows a galleried range; the corresponding range identity, its galleries, facade openings, roof forms and the other buildings' chimney counts are unresolved. Surveyed placements are not moved to fit a compressed retrospective composition.

The compound's composition as a whole — the relative sizes and spacing the print draws — differs from the committed survey, and the other dated pictures of the fort listed on T-2388 have not been read against it at all.

Jail current development trial already exposes the retained core, but whole core/roof and source/camera differences remain; the older merged prose claiming no separate boardstock is stale, because stock already exists.
